description: Los Alamos National Laboratory flies energetic particle detectors (the Combined X-ray Dosimeter, CXD, and the Burst Detector Dosimeter, BD) on GPS satellites, and the public release of their electron and proton measurements is archived by NOAA NCEI. The archive holds several data versions, the latest being version 1.10 revision 2, updated in August 2026, with folders for more than thirty GPS satellites (labelled ns41 to ns81) and a readme of about 660 KB. The data give fluxes of energetic electrons and protons in medium Earth orbit along the GPS orbits, with derived parameters, over many years since about 2000. Coverage: the GPS constellation orbit, global, from about 2000 to recent years. Format and access: files per satellite in public HTTPS directories at NCEI, free. Caveats: the release lags real time; instrument calibration differs between versions, so use the latest; it is a science product and the readme should be read before use. Simulation uses: radiation environment for satellite anomaly and GNSS outage studies, and for space weather hazard scenarios such as the May 2024 storm. Related records: data-c-swims-satellite-sep-vulnerability-inputs uses space radiation inputs for satellite vulnerability; data-donki lists space weather events; data-igs-gnss-products gives GNSS orbits and clocks.
